title: How to set up events in PostHog
description: Practical PostHog event setup — autocapture vs custom capture, identify, and when the heavier SDK is worth it on marketing pages vs the product app.
quickAnswer: **PostHog** can autocapture many clicks, but durable product analytics still needs a small set of **named custom events** plus **identify** after login. Prefer the full SDK in the app; think twice before loading it on a lightweight marketing homepage.

sections.title: Autocapture vs custom events
sections.content:
Autocapture is great for exploration and debugging. It is a poor long-term contract for funnels — CSS and copy changes rename "events" out from under you.

Define a short list of **product events** you will keep for a year (`signup_completed`, `project_created`, `invite_sent`) and capture those explicitly.

sections.title: Identify users after login
sections.content:
Call `identify` with your user id once the session is authenticated so anonymous pre-login events merge into the person profile. Without that, retention and funnels across signup break.

Group analytics (organizations/workspaces) needs a parallel group identify pattern when you bill or report by account.

sections.title: Where to load the script
sections.content:
PostHog’s default web bundle is in our **heavy** [script performance](/learn/analytics-script-performance/) cluster. That is often acceptable inside a SaaS app. On a content marketing site that only needs pageviews, prefer Plausible/Fathom (or a thinner PostHog config) and keep PostHog for the product.

See [PostHog vs Plausible](/compare/posthog-vs-plausible/) for the category split.

sections.title: QA checklist
sections.content:
1. Fire each custom event once in a staging project.
2. Confirm properties types (strings vs numbers).
3. Verify identify merges pre/post login.
4. Recheck quota so autocapture is not burning the bill.

Then build one funnel that matches a real weekly decision — not twelve unused insights.
